source_text: καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ ⸀πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ⸀σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας,
english_snapshot: And without weakening in faith[b][a], he considered his own body as good as dead—since he was about a hundred years old—and the deadness of Sarah’s womb.

signals.text: Or, in another textual tradition: 'he did not consider his own body, which was as good as dead.'

source_text: Δικαιωθέντες οὖν ἐκ πίστεως εἰρήνην ⸀ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
english_snapshot: Therefore[a], since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus the Messiah[c][b],

signals.text: Or, in some manuscripts, 'let us have peace with God.'

source_text: Οὐδὲν ἄρα νῦν κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ ⸀Ἰησοῦ·
english_snapshot: Therefore[b][a], there is now no condemnation for those in Messiah Jesus.

signals.text: Some later manuscripts add: 'who do not walk according to the flesh.' The earliest Greek witnesses support the shorter reading here.

source_text: ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν ⸀σε ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου.
english_snapshot: For the law of the Spirit of life in Messiah Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and death[a][b][c].

source_text: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τοῖς ἀγαπῶσι τὸν θεὸν πάντα ⸀συνεργεῖ εἰς ἀγαθόν, τοῖς κατὰ πρόθεσιν κλητοῖς οὖσιν.
english_snapshot: And we know that for those who love God, all things work together for good—for those who are called according to purpose.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'God works all things together for good.'

source_text: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰδότες τὸν καιρόν, ὅτι ὥρα ⸂ἤδη ὑμᾶς⸃ ἐξ ὕπνου ἐγερθῆναι, νῦν γὰρ ἐγγύτερον ἡμῶν ἡ σωτηρία ἢ ὅτε ἐπιστεύσαμεν.
english_snapshot: And do this[a], knowing the time, that it is already the hour for you to awaken from sleep[b], for now our salvation is nearer than when we believed.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'us' instead of 'you' in 'it is already the hour for you to wake from sleep.'

source_text: Σὺ δὲ τί κρίνεις τὸν ἀδελφόν σου; ἢ καὶ σὺ τί ἐξουθενεῖς τὸν ἀδελφόν σου; πάντες γὰρ παραστησόμεθα τῷ βήματι τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ,
english_snapshot: But you[a], why do you judge your brother? Or you also, why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of God[b],

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “the judgment seat of Christ.”

english_snapshot: Greet Mary[a], who has worked very hard for you.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'for us' or 'among you' instead of 'for you.'

source_text: ἀσπάσασθε ⸀Ἀμπλιᾶτον τὸν ἀγαπητόν μου ἐν κυρίῳ.
english_snapshot: Greet Ampliatus[a], my beloved in the Lord.

signals.text: Greek name form may also be represented as 'Amplias'; the SBLGNT reading here supports 'Ampliatus.'

source_text: ⸂Ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν.⸃ ⸀Ἀμήν.
english_snapshot: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you[b][a]. Amen.

signals.text: Some manuscripts include this verse, while others omit it; many modern editions bracket it as a textual variant in the closing of Romans.

source_text: Τῷ δὲ δυναμένῳ ὑμᾶς στηρίξαι κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου καὶ τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν μυστηρίου χρόνοις αἰωνίοις σεσιγημένου,
english_snapshot: [A] to him who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus the Messiah, according to the revelation of the mystery kept secret for long ages,

signals.text: Verses 25–27 form a closing doxology that appears in different locations across ancient manuscripts. It is found at the end of chapter 14 in the Byzantine majority tradition, after chapter 15 in the earliest surviving papyrus, and here at the end of chapter 16 in major 4th-century manuscripts and the Latin tradition. Some manuscripts include it in multiple places, while a few omit it entirely. Most modern translations retain it here as the conclusion to Paul's letter.

source_text: φανερωθέντος δὲ νῦν, διά τε γραφῶν προφητικῶν, κατ' ἐπιταγὴν τοῦ αἰωνίου θεοῦ, εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη γνωρισθέντος,
english_snapshot: but[a] has now been revealed, and through the prophetic Scriptures made known to all nations, according to the command of the eternal God, to bring about the obedience of faith,

signals.text: This verse is a continuation of the closing doxology (Romans 16:25–27). See note on Romans 16:25 regarding its placement and manuscript evidence.

source_text: μόνῳ σοφῷ θεῷ, διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. Ἀμήν.
english_snapshot: to the only wise God, through Jesus the Messiah, to whom be the glory forever. Amen.

signals.text: This verse concludes the closing doxology (Romans 16:25–27). As noted at Romans 16:25, the placement and inclusion of this doxology vary significantly across early manuscripts, though it is preserved here in the Byzantine majority tradition.
